text: Harness Summary Generated output: the file map a valid composition of selected items produces. A Harness is never authored. text: Data model Summary Six kinds of item, one file shape, fourteen typed links, clusters for navigation, sources for evidence and a provenance record on everything: this is the whole vocabulary a node needs. The highlighted file shape is the same for all six types; links, provenance and sources are keys in its header. One file shape An item is one Markdown file with a YAML header between --- lines ( AGSC-02-01 ). The YAML is a small, safe subset: no anchors, no aliases, no tags, no flow mappings ( AGSC-02-02 ). The body is CommonMark; headings become anchors and, for the chunk export, cut points; fenced code stays code ( AGSC-02-20 ). Lengths are counted in Unicode code points ( AGSC-02-24 ). Unknown keys are kept and reported as warnings, never errors ( AGSC-02-05 ). text: Introduction Summary AgenticSystemCore turns a folder of Markdown files into a shared memory that people and software agents can both read, check, extend and run: a distributed brain whose meaning, form and rules are published, so any agent anywhere can use it, improve it and build systems from it. The idea Most knowledge that agents use today lives in one of two places: inside a single vendor's memory service, or scattered across documents that no machine can verify. In plain language The directory. content/ holds the items in type folders, content/attachments/<slug>/ holds media, and agsc.config.json is the single configuration file. Nothing else is required. Names. Every item has a slug: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, 1–64 characters, unique in the Bundle. The slug is the file name and the last part of the item's web address. text: Items MUST live at content/<type-plural>/<slug>.md where <type-plural> ∈ concepts , episodes , procedures , lessons , clusters , gates .
title: AGSC-01-02

text: The type key in frontmatter is authoritative and MUST match the containing folder; a mismatch is an error ( AGSC-E205 ).
title: AGSC-01-03

text: content/index.md is the Bundle root document. It MUST carry spec_version , okf_version , title , description and base (the IRI base of every item, AGSC-05-01 ; it MUST equal site.base ; a mismatch is AGSC-E204 ), and it MUST NOT carry type ; it is not an item and does not enter the graph as an item.

text: index.md MAY exist in any folder (OKF reserved). _index.md and README.md MUST NOT be used as items.
title: AGSC-01-05

text: Non-knowledge site pages live in site/*.md , outside content/ . They are rendered but MUST NOT appear in the graph, in search.json or in llms.txt item lists.
title: AGSC-01-06

text: Diagram sources live at content/diagrams/<slug>.diagram . A compiled .svg MUST NOT be committed; it is produced into the build output.
title: AGSC-01-07

text: A slug MUST match ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and be 1–64 Unicode code points long ( minLength / maxLength in the schemas, AGSC-02-24 ) — a grammar that forbids a leading, trailing or doubled - by construction and compiles in RE2, Go and Rust (rc.3, DS-3, blocker B4). It is equivalent to the rc.2 wording ^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$ plus "MUST NOT contain -- ", which remains true.
title: AGSC-01-10

text: The slug is the file stem, the value of id when present, and the last path segment of the item IRI. Slugs MUST be unique across the whole Bundle regardless of folder ( AGSC-E206 ).
title: AGSC-01-11

text: AGSC-04 — Canonicalization and determinism Summary Why two builds anywhere give the same bytes: canonical JSON, NFC text, one time format, fixed sort orders and SHA-256. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.4 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-18. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no body has endorsed it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language The promise. Build the same Bundle twice, on two machines, with two conforming tools: every machine artefact is byte-identical. HTML pages are identical within one tool. How. JSON is written in the canonical form of RFC 8785 (members sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, -0 written as 0 ). Text is NFC-normalised before anything is sorted or hashed. Time is one instant format in UTC, taken from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or the last commit. Every list has a stated sort order. Hashes are SHA-256, lowercase hex. Unicode. The vectors were generated with Unicode 16.0.0; a tool states the version it uses. A run of more than 256 combining marks after one character is refused, so hostile input cannot exhaust memory. text: AGSC-05 — Graph: IRIs, RDF views, SKOS, PROV Summary How items become a graph with web addresses, the three RDF views, the ontology and its alignment to SKOS, PROV-O and Dublin Core, and the byte-level pins. text: AGSC-07 — Composition: the closure algebra and the Harness Summary How a selection of items becomes a verdict and a Harness: the five steps in their fixed order, the seven Harness files, skill packs, ports and saved architectures. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.4 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-18. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no body has endorsed it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language Pick items, get a harness. You select items (by slug, or by re-running a saved architecture). The combiner runs five steps in a fixed order: pull in everything requires reaches (breadth-first), hide what is superseded , refuse any surviving excludes pair, warn on contradicts and missing uses , then wire ports — matching what one item produces to what another consumes . A valid composition yields exactly seven files — a JSON-LD record, a Structurizr model, a Mermaid diagram, an arc42 skeleton, decisio

text: AGSC-08 — Governance: provenance, gates, lints, ledger Summary Who made what and who approved it: provenance, sign-off trailers, gates, the four agent-safety lints, the optional agent lane and the ledger derived from git history. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.4 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-18. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no body has endorsed it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language Provenance on everything. Every item says how it came to be — human, ai-assisted, ai-generated or imported — with the operator accountable for it and, when a model wrote it, which model. Changes are proposals. Nobody writes to the published branch directly, agents included. A change is a pull request with a DCO-Plus trailer; gates run as CI checks; a human ratifies. One narrow, configured, revocable exception exists for a trusted automatic channel. Agent safety. Four lints run on every build: an injection scan over bodies, frontmatter at any depth, attachment text and every prose export; a clean-room check; a check that skills stay inert; and a staleness

text: AGSC-11 — The node boundary: cross-origin access, federation, contribution, surfaces, visibility, retirement Summary Where a node meets the outside: cross-origin access, the nine parts of federation, the plugin contract for every agent surface, visibility, retirement and tombstones. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.4 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-18. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no body has endorsed it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version.
